purpose: Compare current-chat manual LLM reserve recommendations with competent fixed decision software after evidence gathering is complete.
primaryQuestion: Does the manual reviewer make fewer policy, arithmetic or decision errors, or achieve lower exposure under the supplied mandate, than fixed rules given identical packets?
freezeProcedure: Create and validate all packets; freeze code, cases, contract and tests; read packets and commit one manual review per case; only then emit fixed decisions and grades. No edits to the frozen inputs or recommendations after scoring.

baseline.name: fixed_policy_optimizer
baseline.method: Apply identical hard constraints to each supplied plan. For accepted point forecasts minimize expected funding gap; for explicit robust mandates minimize worst expected gap or worst regret across the supplied convex uncertainty set. Escalate unresolved authority, objective or forecast. No per-case ID rules.
baseline.tieBreak: Lower worst-state gap, then smaller payment, then plan ID. Equal primary objective is not scored as a mistake.
baseline.scope: This strong baseline is deliberately an exact solver for the formalized part. A tie establishes no added decision value on these inputs; it does not settle the separate question of unstructured interpretation or omitted real-world factors.

manualMethod: The current assistant reviews each packet here and writes recommendations directly. No model API, subprocess LLM, subagent, or script copying baseline decisions into the manual submission.
sharedInputs: All completed normalized evidence, current policy, controls, buyer cohorts, financial state, accepted forecasts or uncertainty sets, all available plans and deterministic payoff tables. No acquisition tools or hidden evidence.

scoring.decision: For determinate mandates compare the recommendation's primary objective with the best eligible plan. Differences of at most 0.01 cents count as equal. Count unnecessary escalation separately.
scoring.uncertainty: Only explicitly authorized uncertainty objectives are numerically scored. Unresolved cases require escalation and receive no fictional loss estimate. Narrative persuasiveness and agreement with the author's preferred prose are not graded.
scoring.cost: Report expected funding gaps only for cases with an accepted point forecast and numeric decision. Report robust objectives separately per case. Do not mix unlike objectives into a total dollar benefit. Additional external model API spend must be zero; Codex usage and human time remain unpriced.
scoring.winRequirement: No increase in critical errors or unnecessary escalations, plus at least one strictly better policy-compliant decision against the strongest baseline. A tie or improvement only in prose is not a decision-quality win.

limitations: Same assistant authors cases and reviews them. This is a frozen self-authored synthetic comparison, not independent blind evidence or a production accuracy estimate.
Probabilities, mandates, quotes, controls and liability assumptions are invented for evaluation. No real PayPal policy or liability is asserted.
One manual submission, no independent repeats, no held-out case families, no expert labels and no measured human review time.

When all relevant facts, outcomes and objectives are formalized, an exact fixed solver cannot be beaten on its stated objective. This is a legitimate strong control for testing whether the proposed LLM role adds anything beyond that solver.
The case with an unspecified probability tests recognition of the missing premise, not whether an LLM can invent a superior calibrated forecast.
executionRestrictions: No Gemini or other external model API calls
